scope: Theorem 7.2 (Delimiter processors on invariant planes) of the manuscript “Prefix Instructions and Incompressible Flows” (preprints/Prefix-Instructions-and-Incompressible-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8cd581420ec9967a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every machine and finite input, each row below gives an effective smooth mean-zero general force on the unit torus, periodic of period one for t ≥ 1, with all mixed derivatives bounded. Its zero-data solution is unique in the classical periodic class and has uniformly bounded energy. The stated fixed particle enters the stated fixed open set exactly when the machine halts. Processor Initial label Open set Delimiter (1/2, 1/2, 0) (2/3, 5/6)2 × T Delimiter, origin coordinates (0, 0, 0) {x : 2/3 < x1 < 11/12} Separate marker push (1/4, 1/4, 0) {x : 3/4 < x1 < 1} The repeated pulse uses only the machine; a separate loader uses the input. All formulas allow arbitrary fixed positive real viscosity as a parameter; absolute computability uses computable viscosity.
